content: 1. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate should be taken either 2 hours before or 2 hours after other medications to avoid interactions. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors must be used, limit their use to less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 5. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects the metabolism of coadministered CYP3A4 substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for increased or decreased effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 9. Atazanavir increases tadalafil levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Discontinue tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating protease inhibitors (PIs), restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 10. Tecovirimat decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 11. Atazanavir increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. After discontinuing cobicistat, allow a one-week washout period before increasing the temsirolimus dose to its original level. 12. Atazanavir increases teniposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 13. Atazanavir and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism, potentially reducing its antiviral activity. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate. 14. Atazanavir increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. A reduced tramadol dose may be necessary. 15. Atazanavir increases trazodone levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Cobicistat also increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Atazanavir increases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Atazanavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Atazanavir increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Carefully titrate antidepressants to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 19. Tucatinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 20. Ublituximab decreases atazanavir effects through immunosuppressive mechanisms, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 21. Atazanavir increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Atazanavir increases umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 23. Atazanavir increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Atazanavir increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Limit vardenafil to 5 mg per 24 hours or 5 mg per 72 hours, depending on the coadministered inhibitor. 25. Atazanavir increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Atazanavir increases venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Atazanavir increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and verapamil increases atazanavir levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential risk of AV block. 28. Atazanavir increases vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are CYP3A4 substrates; coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 29. Cobicistat increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vinblastine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If withholding the regimen for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor. 30. Cobicistat increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure to vincristine. Consider temporarily withholding the antiretroviral regimen in patients who develop significant side effects. If withholding the regimen for a prolonged period, consider initiating a revised regimen without a CYP3A or P-gp inhibitor.
